bench: Four attempts: a01/a02 dry, a03 aborted on an engine 403 (isolation_violation: an ISOLATED world cannot import an artifact from ITSELF; the harness had called import_fetch with dst == src to make the run read back the bytes it published). Fixed by publishing and then FETCHING the artifact back, which gives the same guarantee without the cross-world import path (MACHINE_READINESS B4); import_fetch stays for genuine producer/consumer pairs. a04 of record: 1512 s wall (ecology 1386 s for 228 runs x 60 generations at N=200 on 12 processes; records 124 s for 228 observations), 1 world, 3 artifacts (mature sources with a maturity block, the fetched-back copy, the permuted controls), 228 records, 228 reachability rows, 0 errors. Reconnaissance (declared in PARENT EVIDENCE before sealing) cost 6 runs x 20 generations and changed the design: mature dose 1 takes over by generation 4-5, so the DOSE ladder could not be the ecological control parameter and the CAP ladder was added (none / 0.25 / 0.05). Bench note: the mature source set is 11 of C3-SFE-03's 12 elites (seed 10 never went general); all 11 score held-out 1.0 on W1_d4 directly, so the mature arms' held-out 1.0 is inherited competence, not search.
disposition_note: Assay capable: the positive control fired (mature dose 32 without the cap takes over in 12/12 by generation 2) and the no-import arm never takes over (0/12, pure-resident share 1.0). The preregistered primary (mature vs permuted control on takeover at dose 4 without the cap, min effect 0.5) is 1.0 vs 1.0, effect 0.0: CAPABLE_NEGATIVE. The preregistered falsification fired in the stated direction -- 'if the permuted control takes over at the same doses as the mature material, capability does not drive takeover: injection mechanics do'.
landscape: Takeover is the DEFAULT, not the exception. Without the cap, any injected material -- competent or not -- owns the population within 3-9 generations at every dose from 1 organism in 200 upward, and the no-import control never leaves pure-resident 1.0. Dose sets the SPEED, not the outcome (mature median takeover generation 4.5 / 3 / 2 at doses 1 / 4 / 32; permuted control 8 / 6 / 3.5). The offspring cap is the only knob that moves the clock: at cap 0.05 takeover comes at generations 15-22 (mature) and 26-57 (control) instead of 2-9, roughly a 4-6x delay, and it is the only setting under which any pure-resident lineage is still alive at generation 60 (5-6 of 12 control runs, 0 of 12 mature runs). It never PREVENTS takeover: 227 of 228 non-zero-dose runs end with the import origin at 0.995-1.0. Origin takeover is not clonal collapse: the distinct-genome share stays at 0.78-0.99 in every arm (lowest under the tight cap, which slows mixing, not diversity), so the population keeps varying while its ancestry is monopolised -- 'diversity collapse' measured on genomes would have missed this entirely. Second reading, not preregistered and flagged as exploratory: the permuted controls are a BETTER search substrate than fresh generation 0 despite scoring 0.0-0.125 directly. With no cap they reach the W1_d4 summit in 4/12 (dose 1), 2/12 (dose 4) and 7/12 (dose 32) against 0/12 for the no-import arm; under the tight cap, which keeps them rare, 0/12. Same-length, same-opcode-multiset genotypes are worth more as raw material than random ones, and they are worth more when they are ALLOWED to take over.
science: MAIN RESULT: population takeover by imported organisms is driven by injection MECHANICS, not by the imported material's capability. Preregistered primary, mature vs permuted-control at dose 4 with no cap: takeover in 12/12 vs 12/12 (effect 0.0 against a declared minimum of 0.5), CAPABLE_NEGATIVE, and the preregistered falsification clause fires as written. The control is matched by construction (the same manifests with their instruction blocks permuted: identical length, opcode multiset, operand words and VM knobs) and verified incompetent (direct held-out on W1_d4: mature 1.0 x11, control 0.0-0.125). Takeover rates: mature 12/12 at every dose and cap; control 11/12 at dose 1, 12/12 at doses 4 and 32. The no-import arm is 0/12 with pure-resident share 1.0 and held-out 0.02-0.17, so nothing about the cell produces takeover on its own. DOSE sets speed only: median takeover generation 4.5 / 3 / 2 (mature, doses 1 / 4 / 32) and 8 / 6 / 3.5 (control); the takeover-prone dose of campaign 2 was never a threshold, because a single organism in 200 is already takeover-prone. THE CAP IS THE CONTROL PARAMETER: offspring_cap 0.25 delays takeover by 1-3 generations; 0.05 delays it to generations 15-22 (mature) and 26-57 (control), and is the only setting leaving a pure-resident lineage alive at generation 60 (control 5-6/12, mature 0/12). Declared battery: 'control takeover below half at the mid dose' FAILED (1.0), which IS the result; 'mature takeover monotone in dose' passed; 'cap slows takeover' passed (median generation 3 -> 5 at cap 0.25, -> 15 at 0.05). Target competence separates cleanly even though takeover does not: mature arms end at held-out 1.0 in 72/72 runs (inherited: the sources already solve W1_d4), control arms at 0.02-0.125 except where search succeeded. ANSWER TO THE DIRECTIVE'S QUESTION ('how much foreign lineage can enter before transfer becomes population replacement?'): at N=200 with tournament 4 and elitism 4, ANY dose >= 1 organism becomes replacement within 10 generations unless a descent cap is applied; 0.05 buys 15-60 generations and partial resident survival; no tested setting preserves the resident population. Every campaign-4 experiment that injects organisms must therefore either apply a cap and report the realized origin shares, or state that it is measuring a replaced population. Must NOT be claimed: that imports are useless (the mature arms solve the target immediately, which is inherited competence, not search); that the control's summits (4/12, 2/12, 7/12 vs 0/12 baseline) are a transfer effect -- that comparison was not preregistered here, is confounded with takeover speed, and belongs to C3-SFE-04's matched corridor design; that takeover implies diversity collapse (distinct genomes stay at 0.78-0.99).
